title: Leave Policy
content:
LEAVE POLICY

All employees are entitled for 20 earned leaves for a financial year.

Process for applying:

Planned leaves for more than 2 days should be intimated at least 30 days in advance 

Leave/s should be applied by the employee on Locomo

In order to utilize leave/s, approval must be obtained from the reporting manager through Locomo. 

If an employee takes medical leave for more than two days, it must be substantiated with appropriate medical documentation. 

Marriage Leave:

Employees planning to take time off for their own wedding should submit their leave request at least one month in advance. These leaves will be deducted from their earned leave balance, subject to prior approval from their manager. Before the commencement of this leave, all work responsibilities should be appropriately transitioned to a colleague or the reporting manager, as per the specific requirements. 

Sandwich Leave Policy Applicability:

title: Leave Policy
content:
Sandwich Leave Policy Applicability:

The sandwich policy's application depends on the balance of leave in your account. 

If you have sufficient leave balance and you're using those leaves, the sandwich policy will not apply. 

Once all leaves in your account have been used up, and you are taking any unpaid leave, the sandwich policy will come into effect.

Example –

If your leave balance is two and you decide to take leave on Friday and Monday, with Saturday and Sunday being non-working days, then the sandwich policy won't apply. In other words, the weekends would be treated as regular days off. 

If your leave balance is 1.5 and you're requesting leave on both Friday and Monday, with Saturday and Sunday as non-working days, then the sandwich policy will apply. This means the weekends will be treated as unpaid leave.

Encashment/Carry Forward

title: Leave Policy
content:
Encashment/Carry Forward

A maximum of 10 leaves can be accrued and carried over to the next year. Any remaining leaves beyond this limit will be uncashed at the end of the financial year 

Please note that the leave encashment is calculated based on the basic salary.

title: Maternity Leave Policy
content:
MATERNITY LEAVE POLICY

This policy is framed in accordance the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (‘Act’) as amended and existing rules named thereunder namely the Maternity Benefit (Mines & Circus) Rules (Rules).  This policy covers maternity benefits for women employees who qualify under the governing Act.

 

Purpose - The intent of this policy is to offer maternity benefits to our female employees during their maternity leave. Our strategy is to assist our female employees by implementing actions that facilitate the shift into motherhood. This policy encompasses benefits before childbirth and after maternity entitlements as per the Act. The specifics are outlined below. 

 

Eligibility - In order to be eligible for maternity benefits, you must have been engaged in full-time employment with us for at least 80 (Eighty) days in the 12 (Twelve) months right before the anticipated date of your delivery. 

 

Permissible Period of leave-

title: Maternity Leave Policy
content:
Permissible Period of leave-

The maximum maternity benefit period will be twenty-six weeks, of which no more than eight weeks should precede the expected delivery date.

For a female employee with two or more surviving children, the maximum maternity benefit period will be twelve weeks, of which no more than six weeks should precede the expected delivery date.

If a female employee legally adopts a child under three months old or uses a surrogate to have a child, the maximum period will be twelve weeks.

In the event of a miscarriage or medical pregnancy termination, a female employee will be entitled to six weeks of maternity benefit upon providing proof.

If a female employee undergoes a tubectomy operation, she will be entitled to two weeks of maternity benefit upon providing the necessary proof.

title: Maternity Leave Policy
content:
If a female employee undergoes a tubectomy operation, she will be entitled to two weeks of maternity benefit upon providing the necessary proof.

For the safety of the employees and in accordance with the Act's provisions, no female employee will be permitted to work during the six weeks immediately following the day of her delivery, miscarriage, or medical termination of pregnancy.

Timely Notice – You shall give timely notice in writing (minimum three months prior to expected date) to your reporting Manager. Such notice shall state the date from which you will be absent from work, not being a date earlier than six weeks from the date of your expected delivery. The notice shall be supported by a certificate from registered Medical Practioner. Further, women employee​ should inform HRD about the re-joining date a week in advance and provide a medical fitness certificate to Human Resources on the date of re-joining.

title: Maternity Leave Policy
content:
Apply Maternity leave on Locomo - To apply for maternity leave, you can request for maternity leave in Locomo along with the duration. Once the same is approved, leave policy and attendance would be automatically updated for the period. 

 

Maternity Pay: Subject to the provisions of the Act, the women employee will be eligible for the complete fixed salary during her maternity leave. Any remuneration component associated with performance will not be a part of this payment. Encashment of maternity leave is not allowed.

 

Forfeiture- If a woman employee works after she has been permitted to absent herself under the provisions of the Act & Rules for any period during such authorized absence, you shall forfeit your claim to the maternity benefit for such period.

title: Working Hours
content:
WORKING HOURS

Scope

This Policy is applicable to all employees of Daffodil Software Ltd & Unthinkable Solution, India.

Office Timings

Reporting Time to work is between 09:00 AM-10:00 AM for everyone except for those who have a prescribed different schedule approved by the function head.

At the start of each workday, employees are required to plan their 9 hours of work and communicate this plan to their team and manager.

Employees should plan for a productive 09 hours work-day / 45 hours work-week.  

Employee should focus and make reasonable efforts to complete the planned tasks during the day. At the end of the day employee should submit report on their day’s work. And in case their planned tasks were not finished they should specify the reasons to their team/manager.

Breaks are essential for employee well-being and are encouraged. However, these should not infringe upon the 9 hours of designated productivity.

title: Working Hours
content:
Breaks are essential for employee well-being and are encouraged. However, these should not infringe upon the 9 hours of designated productivity.

In instances where break times extend beyond the scheduled duration, employees are expected to adjust them in-office time accordingly to ensure the completion of their planned tasks.

An employee could be marked as absent or on short leave in case the employee has not submitted task plan/report or his task does not justify a full day’s work.

In case employee’s work/project is behind schedule, the employee may have to normally extend their time in office to complete their work/project.

All employees of Daffodil and Unthinkable.

To perform extra work that will generate additional billing or productivity for the organization.

To undertake unscheduled work that could not have been completed during the normal work schedule.

PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT PLAN

OBJECTIVE

The objective of a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is to bridge the gap between expected and actual performance of an employee. The PIP aids the employee in rectifying performance or behavioral discrepancies through the combined effort and cooperation of both the employer and the employee.

 

The purpose of this process is to provide a formal structure for revitalizing an employee's performance. Through this process, we aim to establish appropriate expectations, facilitate open and direct communication, closely monitor activities with timely feedback, and eliminate potential external factors such as unclear job responsibilities, ambiguous professional standards, or incongruities with the organization’s culture and values.

 

A PIP is a beneficial strategy for both the employer and employee with the ultimate goal of keeping the business on track.

title: Process for Performance Management and Appraisal
content:
PROCESS FOR PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT

Objective:

 

To provide clarity on the performance management and appraisal process.

 

Scope:

 

These guidelines apply to all full-time employees of the organization.

 

Process:

To ensure a streamlined and effective performance appraisal cycle, the following steps have been outlined for seamless execution:

At the end of each quarter, an automated email is triggered to project managers, prompting them to submit feedback for their respective project reportees.

One month prior to the start of the appraisal cycle, an automated notification is sent to all primary managers, officially initiating the appraisal process.

Employees will receive an email notifying them that the appraisal process has commenced.

  Along with the notification, employees are prompted to complete a self-evaluation form to reflect on their own performance and contributions during the evaluation period.

title: Process for Performance Management and Appraisal
content:
Once all feedback is collected, the primary manager shares the innovation score for each employee, which will be visible to the unit head.

 The unit head reviews the employee’s feedback and details and update the appraisal amount accordingly.

After the unit head update the appraisal amounts, an automated email is sent to both the primary manager and HR operations. The primary manager is then responsible for communicating the appraisal amount to the respective employee.

 HR operations will issue the increment or promotion letter to the employee within 5 working days of finalizing the appraisal amounts.

Following the issuance of the increment or promotion letter, the relevant data is sent to the finance team at the month for processing the updated salary according to the new letter.

title: Process for Performance Management and Appraisal
content:
Appraisal data received by the HR team by 20th of each month till 12:00 PM will be effective for that month’s salary cycle. Employees will receive the updated salary in the following month's payment. If the 20th falls on a holiday or weekend, the preceding working day will serve as the cutoff.

Any increment approvals after this cutoff will be processed as arrears in the following month’s salary cycle. During this period, the updated appraisal details will not be visible to employees in Locomo until the HR team shares the updated inputs with the accounts team.

  Once the appraisal letter is issued within the designated timeline, updated compensation will be reflected in Locomo by the last day of the month i.e 30/31st of the month.

 

Note:

  In case the employee is on long leaves (more than 2 consecutive weeks) the increment will be postponed by the duration of leaves.

 In case of maternity leave, the increment will be postponed by the duration of maternity leave.

title: Process for Performance Management and Appraisal
content:
In case of maternity leave, the increment will be postponed by the duration of maternity leave.

 In case an employee resigns from his current position within a month of his increment, his/her increment will not come into effect and he/she will continue working on the previous salary structure.

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
PREVENTION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT OF WOMEN

1.Background

The Policy is framed in accordance with The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition, and Redressal) Act, 2013 (‘hereinafter referred to as Act’), as amended and existing rules named thereunder namely the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as ‘Rules’). Daffodil Software Private Limited (“Daffodil”) & its Affiliates is dedicated to fostering a work environment that is free from discrimination, hostility, and sexual harassment for all women employees.

2. Purpose

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
2. Purpose

At Daffodil & its Affiliates, all employees and Other Individuals are entitled to a Workplace free from Sexual Harassment, ensuring a respectful and inclusive environment. Any behavior that undermines these principles may lead to disciplinary measures, up to and including termination of employment. Daffodil maintains a zero-tolerance approach towards sexual harassment, regardless of whether the actions are carried out by employees, supervisors, clients, or any other individuals connected to the company.

3. Applicability

This policy is applicable to all Employees and Other Individuals associated with Daffodil and its Affiliates while engaged in official duties at the Workplace. It encompasses all related entities, including their office locations across India and any other sites visited during the course of employment. This policy also applies to transportation services provided by Daffodil or its Affiliates.

4. Definitions

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
4. Definitions

This policy applies to all the Employees and Other Individuals of the Daffodil or its Affiliates while on official duty in the Workplace.

4.1. “Affiliates” means the related entities which are outlined in Schedule A attached this policy.

4.2. “Employees” means any female who is on the payrolls of Daffodil or its Affiliates at the time of the incident.

4.3. “Other Individuals” includes female individuals working under contract (whether part-time, full-time, temporary, or ad-hoc), those engaged on a daily wage basis, apprentices, interns, trainees, probationers, consultants, visitors and any other individuals present at the Workplace.

4.4. “Sexual Harassment” includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behaviour whether directly or by implication namely: —

(i) physical contact and advances; or

(ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or

(iii) making sexually coloured remarks; or

(iv) showing pornography; or

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
(ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or

(iii) making sexually coloured remarks; or

(iv) showing pornography; or

(v) any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.

4.5. “Workplace” refers to all Daffodil & its Affiliates office locations across India, as well as any other locations visited by Employees in connection with or during the course of their employment. This also includes transportation services provided by Daffodil or its Affiliates.

5. Internal Committee

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
5. Internal Committee

5.1. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Act, an Internal Committee (IC) has been constituted to prevent sexual harassment and to receive and effectively deal with complaints pertaining to the same. Details of the members, including their names and contact information, of the IC constituted by the Organisation for its offices at Gurugram, Hisar & other offices are outlined in Schedule B and are displayed at office’s cafeteria notice board and have also been published in the intranet https://sites.google.com/a/daffodilsw.com/hr-policies/ and will be updated on a periodic basis, as and when applicable. The Employer will not form a part of the IC.

5.2. A minimum quorum of three (3) members is required to be present for the proceedings to take place. The quorum must include the Chief Presiding Officer (CPO), at least one members and the external member.

6. Procedure & Guidelines for Complaint of Sexual Harassment

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
6. Procedure & Guidelines for Complaint of Sexual Harassment

6.1. An Employee or Other Individuals may make in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment to Internal Committee or through the assistance of Human Resource Department (HRD) to IC or via email at ic@daffodilsw.com within a period of three (3) months from the date of incident and in case of more than one incident, within a period of three (3) months from the date of last incident. Complaints arising of incidents more than three (3) months old shall not be accepted.

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
6.2. However, the IC may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, extend such time limit of filing a complaint up to a further 3 months, if it is satisfied that bonafide circumstances prevented the aggrieved individual from filing a complaint within the time limit mentioned in point (1) hereinabove. The complaint should clearly mention the name and available details of both the aggrieved person and the respondent. Anonymous or pseudonymous complaints will not be investigated.

6.3. Where the aggrieved Employee or Other Individuals is unable to make the complaint on account of her/his physical or mental incapacity or death or otherwise, his/her representative may make the complaint on his behalf.

6.4. In case the complaint is routed through HRD, the HRD will officially forward the complaint to the IC on prompt basis from the date of making the complaint.

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
6.5. The complainant shall submit a copy of the complaint either physically or through email accompanied by available supporting documents and relevant details concerning the alleged act of sexual harassment(s) including names and addresses of witnesses, if any.

7. Conciliation Process

Before the IC initiates an inquiry, the complainant may request the IC to take steps to resolve the matter through conciliation provided, no monetary settlement shall be made as basis of conciliation. If a settlement has so arrived, the IC shall record the same and forward the same to the organization and provide copies of the settlement to the aggrieved individual and the respondent. In such cases, no further inquiry shall be conducted by the IC.

8. Inquiry

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
8. Inquiry

8.1. In case where a settlement is not feasible or could not be arrived at through conciliation, the IC will conduct an inquiry into the complaint. Additionally, an inquiry may also be initiated if the aggrieved person informs the IC that any terms of settlement has not been complied with by the respondent.

8.2. The IC within 7 (seven) working days of receiving the complaint shall forward one copy thereof to the respondent for obtaining a response.

8.3. The respondent within 10 (ten) working days of receiving the complaint shall file his/her reply to the complaint along with a list of supporting documents, names and addresses of witnesses.

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
8.4. The IC shall consider the reply from the respondent and initiate an inquiry. The complainant or the respondent to the complaint shall not be allowed to bring any legal practitioner to represent them at any stage of the proceedings before the IC. IC shall hear both the complainant and the respondent on date(s) intimated to them in advance and the principles of natural justice will be followed accordingly.

8.5. In the event of failure to attend a personal hearing before the IC by the complainant or the respondent on three consecutive dates (intimated in advance) without sufficient cause, the IC shall have the right to terminate the inquiry proceedings or give an ex-parte decision. However, the IC shall serve a notice in writing to the party (ies), 15 (fifteen) days in advance, before such termination or the ex-parte order.

8.6. The inquiry process shall be completed maximum within the period of 90 (ninety) days from the date of receipt of the complaint.

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
8.6. The inquiry process shall be completed maximum within the period of 90 (ninety) days from the date of receipt of the complaint.

8.7. The IC within 10 (ten) days from the date of completion of inquiry shall provide a report of its findings and recommendation(s) to CPO and Mr. Yogesh Agarwal, Managing Director, and such report and recommendation(s) shall also be forthwith made available to the complainant(s) and respondent(s).

9. Interim relief

During pendency of the inquiry, on a written request made by the complainant, the committee may recommend to a) Transfer the aggrieved individual or the respondent to any other workplace; or b) Grant leave to the aggrieved individual or Grant such other relief to the aggrieved individual as may found to be appropriate; or c) Restraint the respondent from reporting on the work performance of the complainant. Once the recommendation of interim relief is implemented, CPO shall inform the committee regarding the same.

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
10. Disciplinary Proceedings

Pursuant to written recommendation of CPO on the basis of report and findings of IC and subject to the final outcome of the appeal proceedings, if any, (necessary disciplinary proceedings may be initiated against the respondent).

11. Appeals

In case of any decision by the IC is not acceptable to the aggrieved person and/or respondent, they shall be given an opportunity to represent the case to the IC in- person and the same shall be recorded. The decision arrived at thereafter by the CPO of the IC shall be final and binding to both and shall be implemented by HRD. They could further appeal to a court or tribunal as per the law within a period of 90 days.

12. Confidentiality

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
12. Confidentiality

Daffodil & its Affiliates understands that it is difficult for the Complainant to come forward with a complaint of sexual harassment and recognizes the Complainant’s interest in keeping the matter confidential. To protect the interests of the victim, the accused person and others who may report incidents of sexual harassment, confidentiality will be maintained throughout the investigatory process to the extent practicable and appropriate under the circumstances. It is the duty and obligation of the Complainant, Respondent, and Witnesses to uphold the highest degree of secrecy regarding the investigation. They shall not disclose any details of the complaint, investigation, or related proceedings to any individual other than IC. Any breach of this confidentiality may result in disciplinary action or other legal consequences.

13. Punishment for False or Malicious Complaints and Evidence

title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women
content:
13. Punishment for False or Malicious Complaints and Evidence

13.1. If the IC determines that an allegation made against the respondent is malicious, or if the complainant or any other person has knowingly made a false complaint or presented forged or misleading documents, the Committee may recommend that the employer take action against the individual responsible. However, simply failing to substantiate a complaint or provide sufficient evidence will not attract punitive measures under this section. Furthermore, malicious intent on the part of the complainant must be established through an inquiry before any action is recommended.

13.2. In cases where the IC concludes that any witness has provided false evidence or submitted forged or misleading documents during the inquiry, it may recommend that the witness's employer to take appropriate action.

14. Management Rights

Daffodil reserves the right to amend this policy from time to time, without prior notice.

CODE OF CONDUCT

What is Code of Conduct?

Our Code of Conduct (‘Code’) is a document that helps all our allied stakeholders in providing guidance to do the right thing in the right manner. It entails the values and principles that are expected out of us in our relationships with these stakeholders. It is designed to help each one of us to maintain the highest standards of conduct. This guidance document aims to particularly provide clarity in areas that can pose ethical challenges. However, like any guidance document this Code shall not be treated as exhaustive.

 

Scope of the Code

title: Code of Conduct
content:
Scope of the Code

This code shall be applicable on all the current and former employees (permanent and contractual) and business associates of the Organization at the group level. “Business Associate” means clients including past and prospective customers, clients, vendors, commercial partners, independent contractors, investors, advisors, agents, promoters, directors, consultants of the Organization at the group level. Further, it also applies to affiliated parties of such business associates and/ or employees.

Continuous Learning

Trust

 

Code of Conduct for Employees

 

What you can expect from us

Professional Development and Growth

People are the most valuable resources that contribute towards realizing the vision of the Organization. Hence, we endeavor to provide opportunities for professional development at all levels by incentivizing and promoting skill development.

Dignity and Respect

title: Code of Conduct
content:
Dignity and Respect

We treat all our people with dignity and respect, irrespective of caste, creed, gender, religion, region, nationality, appearance or any disability. There is zero tolerance policy against any kind of discrimination or harassment.

Open Dialogue

We endeavor to provide platforms to all our employees to practice open dialogue through which they can freely express their thoughts, share feedback, ideas for betterment of the Organization.

Performance based culture

We endeavor to create a culture where excellence and meritocracy are paramount. We reward people for being innovative in identifying new opportunities, approaches and going an extra mile in their respective profiles.

Health and safety

Safety is the core component of Organization’s responsibility. Organization is committed to the safety and health of employees. Since, our employees are our greatest assets so their health and safety is of prime importance for us.

What we expect from employees

Innovation

title: Code of Conduct
content:
What we expect from employees

Innovation

IT/ ITES is a vertical where advancement and refinement takes place rapidly, therefore, it is encouraged to build and innovate solutions that help the Organization to emerge and grow. Hence, we are always on a look out for people who help us in identifying innovative opportunities and approaches.

 

Agility

Ability to adjust quickly and revitalize in response to a fast moving, swiftly changing and uncertain environment is what we embrace. Therefore, employees are encouraged as well as recognized for adaptation of shifting market conditions efficiently.

Result Oriented

We encourage employees to be proactive and have a solution based approach. We support well-reasoned risk taking, and achieving the end result within defined timelines.

 

Process Oriented

We embrace processes and believe in diligently following them. Processes are regularly monitored, created, tweaked and automated to ensure better productivity and efficiency.

Learning and Sharing

Learning is an ongoing process and prepares oneself for bigger roles and challenges. It is equally important to share the gained knowledge for self and organization’s growth.

Conflict of Interest

Our employees must always behave in the best interests of our Organization and ensure that any commercial or personal affiliation does not cause a conflict of interest with their responsibilities in the Organization. A potential conflict of interest arises when we have several contradictory interests at the same time. Consequently, we must avoid situations where our personal interests could conflict with the Organization’s interests. Conflicts also occur when one receives improper benefits, preferential treatment or a personal or financial interest which is contrary to the interests of the Company. Consequently, Employees are not permitted to engage in any business, connection, or action that might jeopardize the interests of our businesses. Each of us is expected to use good judgment and avoid situations that may lead to potential conflict.

The use of illegal drugs and substances poses serious safety and other concerns in any workplace. We do not tolerate the possession, consumption, or distribution of illegal drugs or substances during official hours.

title: Guidelines for Separation of An Employee
content:
GUIDELINES FOR SEPARATION OF AN EMPLOYEE

In an unfortunate event when an employee decides to separate himself/herself from the organization the following procedure is to be followed:

Resignation should be sent over Locomo

Locomo will automatically calculate the relieving date basis the notice period that is mentioned in the employment terms and conditions

During the notice period, one must continue working with responsibility and deliver the expected results

Three months notice period is mandatory to serve for all employees 

If during the notice period, the resignee plans leave/s on the working days, then LWD will get extended by those number of working days

Resignee shall ensure a smooth handover and knowledge transfer to the existing team member or the replacement if it's in place

2 weeks prior to the expected LWD, HR will send an email to the resignee which will have no dues clearance form, exit interview form, exit procedure ppt, and self-declaration form

title: Guidelines for Separation of An Employee
content:
No dues clearance form will reflect all the assets and documents that are to be submitted to various departments before the LWD. The concerned departments will mark no due in the no dues clearance form as and when the resignee submits assets and documents. Resignee to keep a check on the no dues form and connect with the stakeholders to take follow-ups for timely no dues clearance. 

Employee has be in office on the last working day to submit the assets & the exit formalities. 

If the employee chooses to courier/post the assets to the Company instead of the physical handover of the assets, any expenses incurred by the Company for the same shall be deducted from the employee’s full and final settlement. 

Exit interview form and self-declaration form to be submitted to HR on the LWD 

On the LWD, HR to initiate the no dues clearance mail to all the stakeholders. After receiving the clearance from all the departments, HR issues the experience certificate

title: Guidelines for Separation of An Employee
content:
HR to have an interaction on the LWD to know the overall experience of the journey spent with the organization

Your salary is put on hold post  your resignation and it is settled in the full and final settlement.

HR to settle full and final settlement process within maximum 45 working days after receiving all the no dues clearance

Once all the dues are clear and the clearance confirmation is received, HR (Ops) share full & final sheet over personal email id of the resignee within 20 - 25 working days

Resignee to review the sheet and share acceptance over email

The amount gets transferred on any of the payout day either Tuesday or Friday to the account which was the resignee's salary account during his/her employment with organization

HYBRID WORK POLICY

Overview

This policy outlines the guidelines for hybrid work arrangements at Daffodil Software Private Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘Organization/ We’) and its affiliates. The list of affiliates is enclosed at the end of the policy. The goal is to provide flexibility while ensuring operational efficiency and team collaboration. 

Eligibility

Hybrid work arrangements are available to employees in roles that are primarily focused on technology development, implementation, and support. Eligibility will be assessed by delivery owners or project managers, taking into account the individual's role, the requirements of the team, and the operational needs of the business. Employees in non-technical support departments, such as Human Resources, Marketing, Sales, Finance, and Administration, are subject to work from the office model, unless otherwise approved by their respective manager.

Definitions

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
Definitions 

 For the purposes of this policy, the following terms are defined as: 

Core Hours: The designated time period during the workday when all employees must be available for work-related communications and collaboration, regardless of their physical work location

RM Team: The Resource Management Team responsible for the coordination and communication of long-term scheduling for employees. 

Delivery Owners or Project Managers: Individuals responsible for overseeing the performance and work allocation of tech employees, including the assessment of eligibility for hybrid work arrangements and the creation of work rosters.

Tech Employees: Employees whose primary job functions involve technology development, implementation, support, or any role that directly contributes to the company's technical service offerings or product development. 

Work from Office Model: A work model where employees are expected to perform their duties at the company's office location.

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
Work from Office Model: A work model where employees are expected to perform their duties at the company's office location. 

Work Roster: A schedule created by delivery owners or project managers that outlines the expected on-site and remote workdays for tech employees. 

Terms and Conditions of Hybrid Model

Work Schedule: Tech employees are expected to split their workweek between on-site and work from home, minimum 3 office days as determined by the rosters created by delivery owners or project managers.

Work from Home Request:  Any requests for work-from-home lasting up to one week require prior approval from the manager in advance, along with a valid reason. Such requests should only be granted in exceptional circumstances and must be processed through LOCOMO in advance. For requests exceeding one week, advance approval must first be obtained from the manager and then from the Practice Head (PH) through LOCOMO.

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
Core Hours: All employees must adhere to office hours or respective shift hours as per their project requirements.

Adjustments to Work-From-Office Days: In alignment with our hybrid work model, it is expected that all team members will fulfill their required work-from-office days each week. In instances where you need to take leave for part of the week (e.g., for two days), you are expected to work from the office on the remaining three days.

Technology Freshers: Freshers will follow a work-from-office model for the first year from the date of their joining to facilitate onboarding and integration into the company culture. After completing one year, their roster will be determined by their respective manager.

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content: Tech Resources on Bench: Technical resources who are not currently assigned to a client project commonly referred to as 'on the bench'—are expected to adhere to a work-from-office model. This requirement remains in effect until they are deployed to a project. Should they be unable to follow the work-from-office policy, they must submit a formal leave request.

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
Onsite deployment: Technical resources assigned to a client project are expected to adhere to our hybrid work model. For employees below the Assistant Manager (AM) level visiting client locations, the workweek shall be split in consideration of the three-day office roster. If your project requires fewer than three days per week of on-site presence at the client's location, you are required to balance your workweek by spending the remaining days at Daffodil's office. Employees at the AM level and above who are visiting client locations for three or more days in a week shall visit the Daffodil office premises at least one day a week, except in cases where they adhere to a five-day roster entirely at the client location.

Duties while working from home :

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
Duties while working from home :

The Employee working from home must organize a suitable work environment that allows them to perform all job requirements, e.g., appropriate seating, lighting, writing or typing surfaces, adequate noise control, adequate privacy provisions, no distractions and interruptions like traveling while working, basic safety standards. Some of the guidelines are as follows:

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
To ensure an engaging and interactive discussion during virtual meetings, all participants are required to keep their cameras on. In the event that you have a legitimate reason preventing you from using your camera, you must inform both the meeting host and the team at the start of the call. Additionally, if you encounter any technical difficulties that inhibit your ability to use your camera, please report the issue promptly by submitting a service request to the IT department via the ERP. This will facilitate a swift resolution and help maintain the quality of our virtual communications.

Employees should ensure that within the team, by default one should be connected to google meet/video all the time and would need explicit permission to come out of it.

Employee’s google hangout status must remain visible (not hidden) at all times to ensure accessibility and transparency among team members.

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content:
Employee’s google hangout status must remain visible (not hidden) at all times to ensure accessibility and transparency among team members.

There shall be a coordinated lunch/break time within the teams so that team collaboration is not impacted. 

In the event of an emergency that necessitates a brief departure from work duties, team members may take a break not exceeding 15-20 minutes. Such instances should be rare and must be pre-approved by the respective manager.

Employees should ensure that there is uninterrupted broadband connectivity with minimum 10 MbPS speed on your machine for smooth operations.

Employees should ensure to have arrangements of power back up to avoid the impact of power outages

Employees shall dress up in a professional manner and appropriately while working from home.

title: Dress Code Policy
content:
DRESS CODE POLICY

Objective

Our appearance reflects both us and the company. This policy provides simple guidelines to help employees dress in a manner that is neat, professional, and respectful, creating a positive impression with clients, visitors, and colleagues. While our standard is business casual, attire should always reflect professionalism.

Applicability

All employees of Unthinkable Solutions LLP and its affiliates

Guidelines

1.Workplace Definition 

A workplace is defined as any location where employees are conducting business on behalf of the organization. This includes, but is not limited to:

The organization’s physical office(s)

Off-site meetings or events

Client or partner locations

Remote work environments when visible on video calls or representing the organization in a professional capacity

Any virtual platforms where employees interact in a work-related context (e.g., video conferences, webinars, online presentations)

2.Business Casual Standard

title: Dress Code Policy
content:
2.Business Casual Standard

The standard dress code is business casual, balancing comfort and professionalism. Examples of acceptable business casual attire include:

Collared shirts, blouses, or tops with sleeves

Dress pants, chinos, or dark/neutral jeans (neat, not torn)

Skirts or dresses of knee-length or longer

Sarees, salwar kameez, or kurta with trousers (neat and professional)

Sweaters, cardigans, or blazers

Formal shoes, loafers, closed-toe flats, or clean minimal sneakers

3.Neatness & Hygiene 

Clothing must be clean, wrinkle free, and in good condition (not torn, faded or stained).

Employees must maintain good personal hygiene and grooming standards.

4.Work-Appropriate Clothing

Avoid overly casual, revealing, torn, or otherwise unprofessional clothes. 

Examples of inappropriate clothing: workout wear, shorts, short skirts, crop tops, tank tops, slippers, rugged denim, or clothes with offensive messages/images.

5.Respectful Attire

title: Dress Code Policy
content:
5.Respectful Attire

 Avoid clothing with offensive or inappropriate language, symbols, or statements about politics, religion, or other sensitive topics.

Religious and cultural attire is respected as long as it aligns with workplace professionalism.

6.Events & Social Engagements

During dinners, parties, or other social events with clients/vendors, attire should remain professional and aligned with company standards.

7.Non-Compliance

Instances of inappropriate attire will be addressed on an individual basis. Continued non-compliance may lead to formal disciplinary action as per the company’s HR policies. 

Client-Site Dress Code

When working at a client site, employees must adhere to the client’s dress code in addition to our own.

If the client’s dress code is more formal than our business casual standard (e.g., business formals, suits, etc.), employees are expected to comply fully with the client’s requirements.

title: Dress Code Policy
content:
Before visiting or working at a client location, employees should confirm the attire expectations with their project manager or HR.

Footwear

Employees are expected to wear clean, professional footwear at all times. At client sites, footwear should align with the client’s standards and the formality of the setting (e.g., formal shoes when business formals are required). Slippers, flip-flops, or overly casual footwear are not permitted.

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
ATTENDANCE & SALARY FAQ'S

1. How will my attendance be marked?

Your attendance would be marked as present if at least 9 hours of progress has been added for the particular day.

Progress has to be added

within 4 days i.e. Progress for Friday can be latest updated by Monday

in the same month i.e. Progress for 31st cannot be added on the 1st of next month. This is to ensure salary disbursement on time.

Note: If no progress is added, attendance would be marked as “absent” which would NOT be considered for salary calculation.

Steps for marking attendance are available on the following link. 

2. I missed adding my progress within the defined timeline. How can I update my attendance?

You need to raise a progress request to your current reporting manager.

Once your reporting manager approves the request, you will be able to add the progress for that particular day and your attendance will be automatically updated as present if you add at least 9 hours of progress.

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
Steps for raising a progress request are mentioned in the following link.

Note: You should not manually update attendance as present. This would create unapproved attendance.

3. Why did I not get my entire fixed salary for a particular month? How can I see the calculation?

If your salary days are lesser than number of days in the month, it could be due to the following reasons:

Any day marked as absent will not be considered for salary calculation

Any days attendance which is unapproved for salary calculation

You have exhausted your leave balance. You can view your leave balance from Self (in Your Space)  > Attendance > Leave Register

The Salary days considered for the month can be seen in Attendance in Your Space > Attendance Module > Attendance. 

Click on whichever month you want to see the LOP sheet for. Go to LOP. 

4. How do I mark  my attendance as a half day present/leave?

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
Click on whichever month you want to see the LOP sheet for. Go to LOP. 

4. How do I mark  my attendance as a half day present/leave?

Go to Self (in Your Space)  > Attendance > Leave Management. Click on +New Leave Request button at top right corner. In the Leave Request dialog box that pops, Choose Half Day. Enter the half(first/second) for which you want to raise a leave request.

Kindly refer to the document here

5. Who will approve my attendance requests?

Attendance requests will be approved by your reporting manager.  For  any day to be marked as present, you need to add progress for that day. Steps for updating progress after defined timeline are as follows:

Create a progress request

Approval from your reporting Manager

Add progress for the day approval has been received.

 

Note: You should not manually update attendance as present. This would create unapproved attendance.

6. I am not aligned to any project/training. How will my attendance be approved?

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
6. I am not aligned to any project/training. How will my attendance be approved?

Resource Management Team would assign tasks for such days/hours. You can update the progress on that task for updating of progress. Please connect with the RM team in case the same has not been assigned.

7. How do I know who my current reporting manager is?

You can find the details of your reporting manager by going to Self (In Your Space) > My View > Self > Profile and Checking under “Reporting to” field.

8. I am not able to add progress in my project. Error message says I am not an assigned resource in the project. What should I do?

This is because your alignment in the project has not been made in Manaze for the particular day you are trying to add progress. Please connect with the Delivery Manager/Resource Management team to ensure your allocation is marked in the system. You can check your allocation by going to Self (In Your Space) > Allocation.

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
9. I am not able to add progress for yesterday? Why is the 4 day window not applicable?

This may be because the month has changed. Progress must be updated within the same month for ensuring on-time salary disbursal. So, the attendance of the previous month cannot be updated. If you have missed out on the same, you will need to get approval of progress requests from your manager for updating the progress.

Kindly refer to the document here

10. I have added progress of 9 hours but my attendance is not approved.

This is maybe because of 2 reasons:

You have manually updated the attendance as present before marking the progress. Any manual update of attendance would need approval. So, do not manually update the attendance as present 

Or

The day for which progress was added was for a month where salary has already been processed and the attendance is frozen. In such cases, after adding progress, please raise a ticket to the accounts team for updating of attendance.

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
11. I tried adding progress in the Hierarchy Level. I am getting the error "Can't add progress on the parent level". Why can't I add progress?

Please note that you cannot add progress at a parent level in the Hierarchy view. If a task has a subtask under it, the progress needs to be added only at the child level.

For ex. In the above thread, the progress cannot be entered at Test Hierarchy Task or Test Hierarchy Subtask 1. It needs to be added at Test Hierarchy Subtask 2.

Another way to see the task where you can add progress is to look for the Add Progress button, circled in the above image. If the button is visible next to the task, you can add progress. Else, you need to add progress to it's child task.

12. I am working at a client location. How will my attendance be approved?

For employees working at client locations, the attendance would be marked as “Tour” by default. This is equivalent to Present for salary calculation.

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
If you wish to take leave, you need to raise the leave request and get it approved from your reporting manager.

Note: It is your responsibility to ensure leaves are applied in the system & required approvals are taken in Manaze.

13. I have added my progress for an extra working day(EWD) but have not received the extra amount in my salary?

For any extra working day (on weekends or holidays), once the progress is added ,you need to raise an EWD approval request to your manager. Only once your reporting manager approves your EWD, salary for EWD would be considered.

You can generate the request by updating the attendance as EWD for the required date.

14. My leave was approved by my manager. However, I worked on that day and wish to update my attendance. How can I do that?

If you need to change your attendance from APPROVED LEAVE to PRESENT, you will need to get your progress request approved for that particular day.

title: Attendance & Salary FAQ's
content:
If you need to change your attendance from APPROVED LEAVE to PRESENT, you will need to get your progress request approved for that particular day.

Only once it is approved by your manager, you will be able to add progress for that day to update your attendance as present.

15. My attendance for the previous month was updated after salary disbursal. When will I get my salary for that day?

If your attendance has been updated post salary disbursement cycle, you will need to raise a ticket to the Accounts team to process the arrear for the previous month. The amount would be processed along with next month’s salary cycle.

16. Who do I talk to about my appraisal?

Your People Manager is responsible for your appraisal and other such related concerns at organizational level.

17. What data needs to be verified from my end before my salary is processed?

The following details need to be verified -

No LOP should be there

Salary days should be equal to the number of days in the month

content:
The following details need to be verified -

Salary days should be equal to the number of days in the month

All leave requests have been approved

All attendance requests have been approved

In case an incorrect leave request is raised, the reporting manager can reject the leave request. After that, the employee can again raise the correct leave request which can be approved by the reporting manager.

19. My Reporting Manager accepted my incorrect leave request. What should I do?

In case an incorrect leave request is raised, and the reporting manager has approved it, kindly get an approval over mail from your reporting manager and raise a ticket over Manaze to the PI Team to get it manually updated.

content:

For an appraisal to be effective it is a must for an employee to share his/her acceptance on the shared appraisal letter either over email or in person by signing the appraisal letter. Once this is done, the appraisal data is shared with the finance team for release of salary as per the new letter.

Certain cut-off dates are to be adhered in order to make the appraisal effective from the current month. Whatever acceptance letters/e-mails are received by the HR team by 12 noon of 25th of every month, those increments will be made effective in the current month itself and employee will receive the incremented salary in the coming months salary. In case 25th happens to be a holiday/off-day, the cut-off will be considered to be the preceding working day.

content:
Due to salary processing time any increment approvals coming after this cut-off date will be paid as arrears in the next months salary cycle. In these cases, the appraised amount will also not be visible to any employee on Manaze until the inputs are shared with accounts from the HR team which will happen next month only. 

21. When can I see my incremented salary structure on Manaze?

Incremented salary structure will be reflected only by the last working day of the month.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
AI USAGE POLICY

1.                 Purpose

This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Usage Policy (“Policy”) outlines the principles and guidelines for the ethical, secure, and effective use of AI technologies within Daffodil Software Private Limited and its Affiliates (hereinafter collectively referred to as “Organization”). It aims to ensure that AI is leveraged responsibly to enhance productivity, innovation, and decision-making, while minimizing risks and safeguarding Organizational values. The list if Affiliates is attached with this Policy as Annexure A.

2.                 Scope

This Policy applies to all the employees of the Organization whether employed in a permanent, temporary or contract capacity, including full-time, part-time, casual, seasonal, temporary, government sponsored programs, intern and apprentice (“Employees”) who use AI tools for any office-related work, including but not limited to software development, testing, design, and client-related activities.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
3.                 Usage & Access of Approved AI Tools

3.1.             Employees shall only use AI tools and platforms approved by the Organization through the corporate email addresses as provided by the Organization to the Employee from time to time

3.2.             Currently approved platforms include ChatGPT, Claude, and CursorAI. The Organization reserves right to change this from time to time.

3.3.      Employees are strictly prohibited from using public AI tools or platforms to upload or disclose any confidential information, source code, trade secrets, intellectual property, personal or sensitive data, or any other proprietary or secret information of the Company or its clients. Access to such AI tools shall only be permitted for general research, learning, or reasoning purposes that do not involve the sharing of any confidential or protected information.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
3.4.             Any new AI platform or tool must be vetted for compliance, security, and licensing requirements before use. Approval must be obtained from the AI Compliance Committee. New tools or platforms may only be accessed following written approval from the Committee.

3.5.             AI Compliance Committee shall consist of Tech Head and Head of Security and Networking Team.

4.                 Data Protection and Confidentiality

4.1.           The Employee shall not input, upload, or share confidential data, proprietary code, trade secrets, or client information into any AI tools, including approved platforms.

4.2.             The Employee shall not upload any personal data, personally identifiable information (PII), or sensitive personal data to any AI tools, whether accessed through corporate credentials or otherwise. This restriction includes, without limitation, employee information, customer information, and third-party personal data.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
4.3.         The Employee shall not upload artifacts, requirement documents, contracts, or any client-related materials to AI tools without prior written approval from the AI Compliance Committee and explicit client consent where required.

4.4.        The Employee shall not use AI tools in any manner that violates applicable data protection and privacy regulations, including GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation), DPDPA (Digital Personal Data Protection Act), or client-specific data processing requirements.

4.5.             The Employee shall not connect AI tools directly to proprietary repositories, databases, or internal systems without prior written approval from IT Security and Legal departments.

4.6.             The Employee shall not use unencrypted or non-anonymized sensitive data with AI tools. The Employee shall ensure that AI-generated outputs do not contain plagiarized content and must verify all outputs for accuracy and compliance before use.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
5.                 Quality, Compliance, and Review

5.1.             All AI-generated outputs must be reviewed and approved by the Tech Lead or designated reviewer before implementation or delivery.

5.2.             The review must assess including but not limited to: a) Correctness and accuracy of the output; b) Security vulnerabilities and risks; and c) Performance and optimization standards

5.3.             The Employee shall verify that AI-generated outputs: a) Do not infringe copyright or contain plagiarized content; b) Use properly licensed libraries, frameworks, and third-party resources; and c) Comply with open-source licensing requirements where applicable.

5.4.             AI-generated UI/UX outputs must additionally be reviewed for: a) Brand consistency and design guidelines; b) Accessibility standards (WCAG compliance); and c) Bias, inclusivity, and user experience quality.

6.                 Anti-Bias and Fairness

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
6.                 Anti-Bias and Fairness

6.1.             Bias Assessment: All AI models, tools, and outputs shall be periodically reviewed for potential bias based on factors such as gender, age, caste, religion, disability, or other protected characteristics.

6.2.             Corrective Measures: If bias or discriminatory impact is detected, the concerned system shall be promptly re-evaluated, and corrective measures must be documented and implemented before further use.

6.3.             Continuous Improvement: Training datasets, algorithms, and outputs should be updated periodically and refined regularly to reduce the risk of perpetuating bias.

7.                 Roles, Training, and Oversight

7.1.             The Delivery Owner shall be responsible for overseeing compliance with this AI Usage Policy within their respective teams and ensuring adherence to all provisions outlined herein.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
7.2.             The Employee shall complete mandatory training on responsible AI usage as conducted by Organization from time to time, covering data security, regulatory compliance, intellectual property rights, copyright awareness, and ethical AI practices before using any approved AI tools.

7.3.             The Employee shall participate in periodic refresher training sessions conducted by L&D/Compliance/IT departments to stay updated on evolving AI regulations, security protocols, and best practices.

8.                 Documentation and Audit

8.1.             Employee shall maintain detailed records of all AI tool usage in project documentation, including the tools used, prompts submitted, outputs generated, reviews conducted, and approvals obtained. This documentation shall be retained as part of official project records for audit and compliance purposes.

title: AI Usage Policy
content:
8.2.             The Employee shall log AI prompts and corresponding outputs wherever feasible to establish audit trails and ensure accountability. These logs shall facilitate compliance verification and quality assurance processes.

8.3.             The Delivery Owner shall conduct periodic audits to verify adherence to this Policy, assess documentation completeness, and ensure compliance with security and quality standards. The audit frequency shall be determined by Project Heads in consultation with the AI Compliance Committee.

9.                 Violation and Disciplinary Action

title: AI Usage Policy

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
BIDDING PORTAL TRACKER FAQ'S
1. How do I use the Upwork Tracker? 

Download the Upwork tracker on your system first. You can use this link

https://www.upwork.com/ab/downloads/ 

1. Open the Upwork desktop app.

2. Log into your Upwork account.

3. Select the correct contract.

4. Click the On/Off toggle switch to turn on logging.

5. Click the What are you working on? box to enter a memo and/or activity label.

2. How will my attendance be tracked?

Your attendance would be tracked by the tracker applications provided by the bidding platform (Upwork, guru, etc) or the client for tracking the progress of the work done by the respective employee.

4. How does a tracker application track my attendance?

A tracker application takes random screenshots from the time you login to the time you logout to measure the activity or task completed by you during the period. While running the tracker, please refer to Q18 and Q19 for the Do’s and Don'ts while running the tracker .

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
4. Do I have to work for the allotted time continuously?

The tracker usually takes screenshots and generally a brief break is allowed. The time for the same varies from tracker to tracker and details for the same need to be cleared with the client or the Account Manager, whosoever provides details regarding the tracker.

5. What do I do if I have to do an urgent task not related to the project, (official(interview) or personal(banking))?

In case there is an urgent task not related to the project, such as a personal task(Banking, etc) or an official task(Interview, task related to some other project, etc.) you can turn off your tracker for a short time to perform such a task. Do note that it is necessary to turn off the tracker as the screen is recorded and personal data might be leaked.

6. What should I do in case the client turns off the tracker?

In case the client turns off the tracker, immediately stop working and contact your Account Manager and RM Team for the same.

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
In case the client turns off the tracker, immediately stop working and contact your Account Manager and RM Team for the same.

7. Why is a tracker used?

Tracker is usually used by customers because it helps:

Monitor the productivity

Optimize project deliverables

Enhance data security

8. Do trackers breach security?

Data collected from a tracker is usually stored on a secure cloud, where it is secure from third party attackers or malware breachers. There is no breach of security in a tracker. However, refrain from doing any personal task when the tracker is active. 

9. What should I do if I finish my tasks early?

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
9. What should I do if I finish my tasks early?

The client has a daily scrum for all resources engaged on a tracker project where the resource lists the tasks for the given day that will be completed in the allocated time. For instance, if a resource is allocated for 4.5 hours in a project with a tracker, he/she will be assigned tasks for the day that would be delivered in 4.5 hours only. In case the resource finishes the task in less time, he/she can connect with the client or account manager to discuss any further tasks that need to be delivered. Furthermore, it is acceptable if this is a rare occurrence. However, if it is a regular scenario, raise it to your account manager.

10. I finished my tasks early and no additional tasks are assigned by the client for the day. What should I do?

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
10. I finished my tasks early and no additional tasks are assigned by the client for the day. What should I do?

In case you are assigned a task and you finish it before the allotted time, inform your Account Manager and the RM Team. The variation in the hours will be manually billed to the client. For example, if you have been assigned a task for 9 hours and you finish it in 6 hours, the Account Manager will get it manually processed. In a generic case however, the alignment is usually on a weekly basis ( for example 45 hr/week) and a small variation is allowed which can be manually calculated.

11. I am getting client calls and working overtime to complete the deliveries. What should I do?

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
11. I am getting client calls and working overtime to complete the deliveries. What should I do?

You can run the tracker while in a client call. Ideally, the tracker records screenshots and key logs which are monitored by the client. Hence, if you are in a client call, the tracker should run even during the time for which the client call happens. In case a client asks you to not consider the calls as part of the tracker duration and the calls run for a long time, contact your Account Manager and the RM Team for the same.

12. I am working over my allotted hours but the client is not allowing me to turn on the tracker for the extra hours. What should I do?

In case the client is providing you work that cannot be done in an allotted time, contact your Account Manager or Project Manager. They will review the workload and contact the client in case the workload provided by the client is adequate as per the time or not.

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
13. Who do I contact in case of any issue faced in using the tracker?

You can either contact your Project Manager, or your Account Manager, to address the issues faced in using the tracker.

14. What do I do in case I forget to turn on the tracker while working?

In case you forget to turn on the tracker while working, immediately inform your Account Manager about the same. He/she will guide you through adding manual hours so that they may be approved by the client. 

15. Can my allocated hours on the project change mid-project?

Your Account Manager will inform you and the RM Team in case of any change in your allocated hours on the project. Suppose you are aligned for 4.5 hours on a project from 1-15 September. Your alignment is changed to 9 hours per day from 16-31 September. This will be notified to you by email. 

16. What should I do if I get any mail regarding profile verification on Upwork?

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
16. What should I do if I get any mail regarding profile verification on Upwork?

You can contact the Account Manager if you receive any mail regarding profile verification.

17. I am unable to log hours in the tracker correctly. What should I do?

In case you are unable to log the hours correctly, log out and login to the App. 

18. What are the various Do’s and Don’ts of tracker engagement?

Do’s

Work on Upwork tracker and avoid opening any other window or content which is not related to the project as the tracker takes screenshots regularly of your activity during the time the tracker is on.

Make sure you log/complete assigned hours on a daily basis and complete weekly quota of hours on tracker.

Don'ts

Don’t open any other window or content while working on the project because Upwork tracker takes screenshots every 10 minutes

Don't add any manual hours without informing Account manager

title: Bidding Portal Tracker FAQs
content:
Don't add any manual hours without informing Account manager

Don't make your tracker run continuously if you are not working, you need to turn off the tracker when you have completed your work for the day.

Don't open any personal content such as emails, bank details or explicit content like music, movies etc. while working on a tracker.

Don't work without turning on an Upwork tracker. Any work done without an Upwork tracker will not be billed.

TICKETING
Purpose

This document elaborates the processes associated with Ticketing Workflow in Manaze5.

Ticketing helps you raise concerns to the respective departments where you are facing the concerns.

The Steps involved in the various processes are:

Raising A Ticket

1.	In order to raise a ticket, go to Self view in Space > Tickets. Click on New Ticket.

2.	Enter the subject and description of the issue you are facing for which you have raised the ticket.

3.	Enter the department to which you want to raise the issue.

4.	Choose the category of the issue you are facing.

5.	Choose the subcategory.

6.	Mention the priority of the concern. Please use this diligently so that teams would be able to identify urgent issues separately

7.	Enter the seat number at which you are working. (Currently, Work From home can be mentioned)

8.	Provide an attachment, if any, for the same.

9.	Click on Submit. Your ticket has now been submitted.

10.	You can now see the ticket in your Open tickets.

title: Ticketing
content:
9.	Click on Submit. Your ticket has now been submitted.

10.	You can now see the ticket in your Open tickets.

Viewing the status of the Ticket

1.	You can see the status of your ticket and the concerned agent assigned. You can also check the expected closure time for the ticket. 

2.	Click on a given ticket to see the conversation and the detailed status of the ticket.

3.	The concerned agent will respond to your query. In case you wish to respond to them, type your message in the chat box given. 

4.	In case you wish to loop in someone else in the conversation, click on CC, and add the names of the people you wish to loop in.

5.	Once you’ve entered your message, click on send. Your request is now sent.

6.	If you feel the query has been solved. Click on Mark Closed. Otherwise agent would mark the ticket closed once the resolution is provided.

Reopening Closed Tickets

1.	To view your closed tickets, go to Tickets > Closed.

title: Ticketing
content:
Reopening Closed Tickets

1.	To view your closed tickets, go to Tickets > Closed.

2.	In case you are not satisfied with the resolution provided by the employees, go to the three dots next to the ticket name and click on Reopen.

Your ticket is now reopened for further resolution. 

Submitting Feedback on Closed Tickets

1.	To provide feedback on closed tickets, choose the Submit button under feedback next to the ticket details.T his would be reviewed regularly.

2.	Choose the type of feedback you wish to provide for the resolution offered by the agent.

ATTENDANCE

Overview
This instruction manual will provide you with comprehensive instructions on how to effectively utilize Locomo for managing attendance and ticketing efficiently.

Flow Path :  Locomo > Me > Attendance

The Attendance module in Locomo includes the details pertaining to the employee attendance. It can be accessed by following the above flow path.

Following are the various activities associated with the Attendance Module:

Monthly Attendance Tab :

This tab provides details of  month wise total days, payable days & LOP’s.

Leave Register Tab

Flow Path: Locomo > Me > Attendance  > Leave Register

This tab provides details of month wise leaves available, accrued, consumed & balance available.

Raise New Leave Request
